messages:
Mia (Marketing): Quick sync — we need a compact enterprise-facing one-pager that the sales team can hand to prospects and include in webinar followups. Focus: security controls, SLA options, deployment modes, and two benchmark callouts. Due EOD Tue.
Ollie (Product): Sounds good. I'll pull the canonical SLA wording and the p50/p99 latency numbers for hosted vs dedicated. Want a short table, not an appendix.
Sara (Solutions): Keep diagrams high-level: 1) Hosted API flow, 2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) topology, 3) Private (VPC/on-prem) control-plane callout. One simple icon per mode.
Devon (Sales): For inbound routing, include an assignment rubric: self-serve signups < $5k ARR → MQL nurture; > $5k ARR but no security req → SDR; security/SLAs or private ask → AE + SE. Put example qualification questions.
Jordan (Growth): We'll tie this to next week's webinar. Need a one-pager PDF to attach in the registration confirmation and the post-webinar follow-up email.
Mia (Marketing): Benchmark narrative: two short callouts — 1) latency SLO comparison: hosted p99 ~ 350ms for 512-token completions; dedicated p99 ~ 150ms on reserved pools; 2) cost-efficiency: intelligent batching reduces tokens/unit cost by ~20% on steady workloads. Keep numbers rounded and add a footnote: "workload dependent, average across X models".
Ollie (Product): Add a line: "Smart routing and fallback keep SLAs stable — automated fallback to compatible model variants during capacity spikes." Short but reassuring.
Sara (Solutions): FAQ snippet: "Can we get audit logs?" -> "Yes — KMS/HSM integration + exportable audit logs for Private and Dedicated; hosted offers audit log export for enterprise customers."
Devon (Sales): Suggested subject lines for email follow-up: "Redwood Inference — Enterprise Brief: Security, SLAs, Deployment Options" or shorter "Redwood Enterprise one-pager". Also suggest CTAs: "Request Dedicated Trial" and "Schedule Private deployment consult".
Mia (Marketing): Creative direction: 1 page, single column. Top banner: one-line value prop. Left column: bullets for security and compliance (KMS, SOC2, VPC, data separation). Middle: SLA & performance bullets + 2 small benchmark callouts. Right: deployment modes with tiny diagrams + CTAs. Bottom: inbound routing note for sales.
Jordan (Growth): For webinar registration flow: attach one-pager, then for registrants who answer "interested in enterprise" -> set lead score + route to AE. Also add a short gate question: "Do you need private deployment or dedicated capacity?"
Ollie (Product): FYI — don't publish raw model names or exact kernel tuning numbers. Keep performance claims at a high level and add a link to the benchmarks page for deeper detail.
Mia (Marketing): Can someone draft the copy today? I'll assemble design. Talking points I want: "Predictable latency, deployment flexibility, built-in enterprise controls, cost levers you can tune." Keep it punchy.
Sara (Solutions): I'll drop 3 qualifying questions for the routing section: 1) "Is data regulated?" 2) "SLA target (uptime/latency)?" 3) "Preferred deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)?"
Devon (Sales): Add an inbound sample routing rule for HubSpot: tag=enterprise -> owner=AE-team; if tag=private -> priority=High; if ARR_est>50k -> immediate AE outreach.
Mia (Marketing): Great — I'll convert this thread into a draft doc and ping design. Ops-bot, create shared doc in marketing drive please. :pray:
ops-bot: New document created: /marketing/enterprise-onepager-draft-1768001234 (access: marketing, product, sales)
Jordan (Growth): Timeline check — draft copy by EOD today, design mock by tomorrow morning, final PDF by Tue EOD for webinar assets.
Mia (Marketing): Thanks all. I'll post the assembled PDF here when ready and include the exact inbound routing snippet for HubSpot. :thumbsup:
